Every instinct in him screamed to move, but she had him locked. One arm was iron across his sternum, the other pulling his abdomen as close as she could manage. Another hitch moved through him, sharper than the last, and his better judgment lost the argument. His hands found her wrists and pried, feet kicking for purchase, the animal logic of up, out, surface overriding everything else with a completeness that left no room for logic or reason. The current caught them from the side, almost dragging him out of her grip. She felt the twitch of a choice — that split second of fight or surrender — and chose for him. She didn’t stop to think. Just reached up and clapped her palm over his mouth and nose, fingers trembling with pressure, as she wrenched his head back against her shoulder to keep him from twisting away. She felt him register it. Felt the half second where he understood what she was doing and why. The next second, he exploded. His whole body torqued against her grip, one hard convulsive effort, hands clawing at her wrist, legs kicking at nothing. She held on. she wouldn’t lose him. Not like this. If he tore away now, they may never find him again. She needed to not lose him to the dark. She could deal with the fallout later. He bucked again, weaker, the reserves going fast, the water indifferent to how much he had left or how much he needed. She pressed his head back and held him flat and felt his chest seize against her palm, willing him to stop spending what he didn't have. Stop. Stop. Just stop. Please just pass out... His chest seized against her once, then again. She tightened her grip and held him there, a last blockade against the water, until the last jerk rolled through him like an aftershock — and stopped. She adjusted her grip and went still with him. Let her heart keep hammering against the fragile shape of his back. No wasted motion. Just a silent prayer that she hadn't just made the worst decision of the night. David felt every kick in his teeth. The concussive thud of each impact travelled up through the water and into his jaw, his chest, the base of his skull. Terror burned hotter than exhaustion now, driving his legs back into the planks over and over. The wall was talking back now in a way it hadn't been before, something in the structure of it shifting under the assault, the flex coming back different from the dead resistance of earlier. Jake had him. That was the other thing he could feel — the grip on his upper arm, firm and present, the anchor that kept the current from sweeping him out of the alcove every time the recoil took his footing. He didn't make any motion to acknowledge Jake there. Couldn't afford the shift in focus. The grip shifted. He felt it happen — the tight clamp of a hand around his arm loosening by degrees, reorganising, fingers finding the fabric of his sleeve instead. He didn't look. He hit the wall again and felt Jake adjust behind him with a small tremor and filed that away too, in the same place he'd filed the sparks at the edge of his vision that had been there for the last three kicks and weren't getting better. He shook off the sparks. He knew what they meant. He'd felt that particular warning before, in other contexts, and he filed it in the same place he'd filed Jake's shifting grip and the way his lungs had been sending strongly worded letters of protest. He re-braced. Drove his heels into the wall. The vibration that came back was different — not the solid protest of before but something finer. A true sound this time. Short, fragile, but cutting through everything with a single distant crack. He felt it in his feet. Felt the board flex inward and catch. There. His chest hitched once as he backed against the wall for another kick. David’s heart stuttered. He hauled himself back into position, boot slipping slightly— His anchor had vanished. Jake’s grip slid from his arm and dissolved into the black. David whipped his head around, shot a hand after him, and hit only water. He held the reach for one suspended beat — Jake — and then let his arm drop and put his back against the wall and found the angle again. No time. No point. Refocus. Either Jake had been swept. Or he— no. No. If the wall didn't come down, none of it mattered. None of them. The board had cracked. He'd heard it. He could feel the flex in it had changed, the resistance giving way to something that felt almost like progress, and there was nothing left in the world except that and the next kick and the one after that. Either the wall was breaking— Or they all were. Ch 11 – Emergence Outside, the school was quiet. The playground lay still in the perpetual night air, long shadows cast by nearby streetlamps highlighted half-rusted jungle gyms and faded spring riders in a sick yellow glow, the gentle chug of partially finished generators echoing through the otherwise silent domain. The only thing different than the usual calm was the water. It seeped through the cracks in the boarded wall in thin dark trails, following gravity down the planks and pooling in the mud below. The boards were dark with it, saturated, the wood swollen past its original shape. A low thump rolled through the wall from the inside. Heavy. Close.
